The Lord wants to see whether you will perform what he told you to do even when things do not work out how you planned; that is what proves you faithful in temptation and worthy of being exalted. Saul failed that test in the time of his distress.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

And it grieved Samuel, and he cried unto the Lord all night. Pride had to be in operation for Saul to transgress on that level, and pride is where the throne is lost.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

note.label: Character & Integrity: The Hidden Strength Behind Wisdom

points: Saul deflects again, the same blame game as chapter 13: They have brought them from the Amalekites, for the people spared the best of the sheep and of the oxen, to sacrifice unto the Lord thy God; and the rest we have utterly destroyed. Verse 9 already told us Saul and the people spared them; now suddenly it is only the people, and for a good reason, a sacrifice, as though the Lord ought to be pleased.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

points: And Saul said unto Samuel, Yea, I have obeyed the voice of the Lord. Wait a second. Remember we read earlier in Corinthians about those that sinned and repented not. So Saul's initial response, was that a sign of godly sorrow? No. There was none involved.

note.label: The Building Blocks of Bitterness

points: Wherefore then didst thou not obey the voice of the Lord? Saul answered, Yea, I have obeyed the voice of the Lord, and have brought Agag the king of Amalek. Wait a minute: the king is still alive. Saul is playing the defensive, justifying his actions, making excuses.

note.label: The Bold and the Bashful

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

points: And Saul said, I have sinned: because I feared the people, and obeyed their voice. If you are a leader and you are in fear of your people, what can those people do to you? Manipulate you. You are a pushover; they can sway you left and right. Who is supposed to move you? The Lord, not the people you are supposed to lead. You are not leading the people; you are being led by the people.

note.label: The Bold and the Bashful

points: Samuel refuses: I will not return with thee; for thou hast rejected the word of the Lord, and the Lord hath rejected thee from being king over Israel. Think it through: Samuel gave Saul the opening at the bleating of the sheep, and Saul would not humble down; he asked why Saul disobeyed the voice of the Lord, and Saul justified himself again. Two admonitions were given and refused before this rejection.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

points: That is the spirit of vanity, caught up in a rank and a title while forgetting that the title came for pleasing the Lord; once you discontinue pleasing the Lord, the title is going to leave as well. So Samuel turned again after Saul, and Saul worshipped the Lord.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

points: Then Samuel went to Ramah, and Saul went up to his house in Gibeah, and Samuel came no more to see Saul until the day of his death: nevertheless Samuel mourned for Saul, and the Lord repented that he had made Saul king over Israel.

The mourning is what makes it sad: Samuel raised Saul up from nothing, saw his potential, and saw the Spirit come upon him in chapter 11 when he stood up as a savior for the people; he had hope in him, and it came to this. Samuel was grieved, and the Lord repented of the appointment.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

points: King David was chosen although King Saul was still in power.

But the spirit of the Lord departed from Saul. If the spirit of the Lord is not occupying your fleshly body, what replaces it? Evil spirit, demons, legions. The works of the flesh, those are demons: envy, hatred, malice, guile, strife, demons. So if the spirit of the Lord left Saul, an evil spirit entered in unto him.

Even the servants knew: yo, this got the devil on him. Sometimes it'll take some people, whether they have rank or not in the congregation, to recognize the fault of some of the leaders, because men tend to go off. We look at many of these congregations like, nobody checks what he's saying? Nobody sees that this man has a ball and chain in his hand with a cup of cognac right here? Nobody sees he's talking with a lisp and flicking his hair, the evil gay spirit on this dude, meanwhile he's calling everybody else gay? Nobody sees the hatred on this man, constantly talking about another man's wife, constantly talking about the color of our uniform? But the servants of Saul seen it. So the servants of Saul are much better than some of the around today.

note.label: The Inevitability of Obsolescence & Agony of Defeat

points: Recall the class on chapters 12 through 15: in chapter 15 Saul rebelled against the commandment, and after two admonitions he still would not humble down and repent, so the Most High rejected him from reigning over Israel and told him through Samuel that his kingdom would not continue.
Samuel had groomed Saul up and saw potential in the brother, so he mourned over him; the Most High asked how long he would keep crying over the man he had rejected.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

points: Samuel feared that Saul would kill him if he heard of it. Remember the influence and love Samuel had among the people; even so, this shows the power of the king. Saul raised no hand against Samuel yet, but a king had the authority to command a prophet's death.

The Most High told Samuel to go in with a heifer, as if coming only to sacrifice; he would go incognito, not letting it be known that he was coming to anoint Saul's replacement, and the Most High would show him whom to anoint.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

points: Simultaneously, as the Most High put his spirit on David, the spirit departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord troubled him. Note it well: the evil spirit came from the Lord; that is a teaching the church world leaves out.

Chapter 15 said rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and Saul is now headed down that downward spiral; the spirit is leaving him, and he will eventually become a reprobate and dabble in real witchcraft.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

points: Saul's servants could see it: behold now, an evil spirit from God troubleth thee. It was evident; whatever he was doing and saying, his servants could tell an evil spirit was on him.

Why did the spirit leave Saul? Wisdom walks with a man by crooked ways at the first and tries him by her laws. Saul was put through a trial, whether he would keep the commandment given through the mouth of the prophet, and he went wrong; so the spirit forsook him and he was given over to his own ruin, that abyss of jealousy, envy, and hatred.

note.label: 1 Samuel 24: David Spares Saul in the Cave at Engedi

points: David also took Ahinoam of Jezreel, and they were also both of them his wives; but Saul had given Michal his daughter, David's wife, to Phalti the son of Laish, which was of Gallim.

note.label: 1 Samuel 25: Nabal's Folly and Abigail's Wisdom

points: The Ziphites came unto Saul to Gibeah, saying, Doth not David hide himself in the hill of Hachilah, which is before Jeshimon? Right here we are going back: chapter 26 is picking up on what we read in chapter 23, when the Ziphites first went up to Saul to deliver David into the king's hand.

note.label: 1 Samuel 26: David Spares Saul a Second Time

points: Saul arose and went down to the wilderness of Ziph, having three thousand chosen men of Israel with him, and pitched in the hill of Hachilah; but David abode in the wilderness, sent out spies, and understood that Saul was come in very deed.

note.label: 1 Samuel 26: David Spares Saul a Second Time

points: David beheld the place where Saul lay, with Abner the son of Ner, the captain of his host; Saul lay in the trench with his spear stuck in the ground at his bolster, and the people pitched round about him as protection to the king.

note.label: 1 Samuel 26: David Spares Saul a Second Time

points: David asked Ahimelech the Hittite and Abishai the son of Zeruiah, the brother of Joab, Who will go down with me to Saul to the camp? and Abishai said, I will go down with thee; and they came to the people by night, and all lay sleeping.

note.label: 1 Samuel 26: David Spares Saul a Second Time

points: This is when Saul was hunting David to kill him, because Saul was dealing with bitterness, envy, and hatred. David and Abishai came down to the camp by night, and Saul lay sleeping in the trench, with Abner, the top warrior in Israel at that time, and the people round about him.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness Part 2

points: They took the spear and the cruse of water from Saul's bolster and got them away, and no man saw it, nor knew it, neither awaked, for they were all asleep, because a deep sleep from the Lord was fallen upon them.

note.label: 1 Samuel 26: David Spares Saul a Second Time

points: Then said Saul, I have sinned: return, my son David... behold, I have played the fool, and have erred exceedingly. David hit a nerve, and Saul caught himself. Sometimes people do evil to you because Satan jumped on them, and afterward they realize it and say, I am sorry. When somebody comes at you sideways, it is not necessarily the person in front of you that you are fighting; it is Satan in them.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness Part 2

points: Saul said, I have sinned: return, my son David, for I will no more do thee harm, because my soul was precious in thine eyes this day: behold, I have played the fool, and have erred exceedingly. Saul was acknowledging once more David's righteousness, because again David had an opportunity to kill Saul and did not put forth his hand.

That is what we have to get to as far as brotherly love: when we see each other, we see Christ in each other. That is what our nation is lacking, and that is why we have to be that example, as David was in sparing Saul's life.

note.label: 1 Samuel 26: David Spares Saul a Second Time

points: David said in his heart, I shall now perish one day by the hand of Saul: there is nothing better for me than that I should speedily escape into the land of the Philistines, and Saul shall despair of me, to seek me any more in any coast of Israel.

note.label: 1 Samuel 27: David Dwells in the Land of the Philistines

points: Samuel was dead, and Saul had put away those that had familiar spirits and the wizards out of the land. The Philistines gathered themselves together, and when Saul saw the host of the Philistines, he was afraid, and his heart greatly trembled.

note.label: The Bold and the Bashful

points: And when Saul enquired of the Lord, the Lord answered him not, neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets. The Lord was not dealing with Saul anymore.

note.label: The Bold and the Bashful

points: Then said Saul unto his servants, Seek me a woman that hath a familiar spirit. Saul just rid the land of all the soothsayers, the familiar spirits, and the wizards; now he says find me one so I can know what is going on. His mind is all over the place; he is double-minded.

note.label: The Bold and the Bashful

points: And Saul disguised himself, and put on other raiment, and came to the woman by night. And the woman said, Behold, thou knowest what Saul hath done: wherefore then layest thou a snare for my life, to cause me to die?

note.label: The Bold and the Bashful

points: What Saul was doing when he went to the woman with the familiar spirit is called necromancy. Look that word up: it is when you go to somebody that conjures up spirits.
Saul turned to this because the Lord was departed from him and answered him no more, neither by prophets nor by dreams, so he had Samuel conjured up to tell him what to do.

note.label: 1 Samuel 28: Saul and the Woman with the Familiar Spirit

points: Saul fell straightway all along the earth, sore afraid because of the words of Samuel, and there was no strength in him, for he had eaten no bread all the day nor all the night.

The chapter in sum: Saul inquired of the Lord and was not answered, so he turned to a woman with a familiar spirit and conjured up Samuel. Samuel told him that because of his disobedience the Lord was not dealing with him anymore, and prophesied that tomorrow Saul and his sons would be with him.

note.label: 1 Samuel 28: Saul and the Woman with the Familiar Spirit

points: The princes remembered the song: is not this David of whom they sang one to another in dances, saying, Saul slew his thousands, and David his ten thousands?

note.label: 1 Samuel 29: Never Trust Thine Enemy

points: The battle went sore against Saul, and the archers hit him, and he was sore wounded of the archers.

note.label: 1 Samuel 31: The Death of Saul

points: Saul said unto his armourbearer, Draw thy sword, and thrust me through therewith; lest these uncircumcised come and thrust me through, and abuse me. What Saul was fearful of is what you see in war, how men will abuse their captives, killing them and abusing their bodies. He was already wounded and could not get away, so instead of being taken captive he told his armourbearer to kill him.

His armourbearer would not, for he was sore afraid; therefore Saul took a sword and fell upon it, and when his armourbearer saw that Saul was dead, he fell likewise upon his sword and died with him. So Saul died, and his three sons, and his armourbearer, and all his men, that same day together.

Remember what we read in chapter 28: when Saul went and conjured up the spirit of Samuel, Samuel said to him, To morrow shalt thou and thy sons be with me. He prophesied unto Saul what was going to happen, and now we read the fulfillment of that prophecy.

note.label: 1 Samuel 31: The Death of Saul

points: When the men of Israel that were on the other side of the valley, and they that were on the other side of Jordan, saw that the men of Israel fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, they forsook the cities and fled, and the Philistines came and dwelt in them.

note.label: 1 Samuel 31: The Death of Saul

points: So in chapter 31 we read of Saul and his sons and his armourbearer dying at the hands of the Philistines. This concludes the history of Saul coming to an end; the second book of Samuel takes up the rise and much of the history concerning King David.

note.label: 1 Samuel 31: The Death of Saul

points: When the inhabitants of Jabeshgilead heard of that which the Philistines had done to Saul, all the valiant men arose and went all night, and took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons from the wall of Bethshan, and came to Jabesh and burnt them there. They took their bones and buried them under a tree at Jabesh, and fasted seven days.

note.label: 1 Samuel 31: The Death of Saul

points: After the death of Saul, when David had returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites and abode two days in Ziklag, a man came out of the camp of Israel with his clothes rent and earth upon his head, and fell to the earth before David to do him honor.

note.label: 2 Samuel 1: David Laments Saul and Jonathan

points: David asked him how the matter went, and he answered that the people were fled from the battle, many had fallen and were dead, and Saul and Jonathan his son were dead also.

note.label: 2 Samuel 1: David Laments Saul and Jonathan

points: The young man told David that he had come by chance upon mount Gilboa, and found Saul leaning upon his spear with the chariots and horsemen pressing hard after him. In the earlier account Saul fell upon his sword but did not die at that moment.

note.label: 2 Samuel 1: David Laments Saul and Jonathan

points: David took hold on his clothes and rent them, and all the men with him did likewise, and they mourned and wept and fasted until evening for Saul, for Jonathan, and for the house of Israel that were fallen by the sword.

note.label: 2 Samuel 1: David Laments Saul and Jonathan

points: David's lament is a prophecy given in the spirit, almost a eulogy: Saul and Jonathan were lovely and pleasant in their lives, and in their death they were not divided; they were swifter than eagles and stronger than lions. Before the devil jumped on Saul he was good, and the two of them were good together.

note.label: 2 Samuel 1: David Laments Saul and Jonathan

points: David sent to the men of Jabeshgilead who had buried Saul, blessing them for the kindness shown to their lord, and telling them Judah had anointed him king over them.

note.label: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah

points: Abner the son of Ner, captain of Saul's host, took Ishbosheth the son of Saul and made him king over Gilead and Israel; Ishbosheth was forty years old and reigned two years, while Judah followed David. David reigned in Hebron over Judah seven years and six months.

note.label: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah

points: There was long war between the house of Saul and the house of David, but David waxed stronger and stronger and the house of Saul weaker and weaker. Each had those that followed him, but the Most High increased David because he had been anointed to be the next king over Israel.

note.label: 2 Samuel 3: The House of David Waxes Stronger

points: Abner made himself strong for the house of Saul. When Ishbosheth charged him over Rizpah, Saul's concubine, Abner was very wroth, saying he had shown kindness to the house of Saul and not delivered them to David, and now was charged with a fault concerning this woman.

note.label: 2 Samuel 3: The House of David Waxes Stronger

points: Abner swore to do to himself and more, to translate the kingdom from the house of Saul and set up the throne of David over Israel and Judah, from Dan even to Beersheba. Ishbosheth could not answer him a word, because he feared him. Abner was through with Ishbosheth and turned to go with David and the Lord.

note.label: 2 Samuel 3: The House of David Waxes Stronger

points: Abner sent messengers to David offering to bring all Israel to him. David agreed to make a league, but required that Michal, Saul's daughter, first be brought to him, and he sent to Ishbosheth to deliver his wife whom he had espoused for a hundred foreskins of the Philistines.

note.label: 2 Samuel 3: The House of David Waxes Stronger

points: When Saul's son Ishbosheth heard that Abner was dead in Hebron, his hands were feeble and all the Israelites were troubled.

note.label: 2 Samuel 4: The Slaying of Ishbosheth

points: Jonathan's son Mephibosheth was lame of his feet. When the tidings came of Saul and Jonathan out of Jezreel, he was five years old, and his nurse took him up and fled, and in her haste he fell and became lame.

note.label: 2 Samuel 4: The Slaying of Ishbosheth

points: Rechab and Baanah escaped, having smitten and slain him on his bed; and they beheaded him and took his head and got away through the plain all night, and brought the head to David at Hebron, saying, Behold the head of Ishbosheth thine enemy, and claiming the Lord had avenged the king this day of Saul and his seed.
They did too much; they went overboard. Israel being out of order took the matter upon themselves. David had no quarrel with Saul's sons; it was Saul who sought his life.

note.label: 2 Samuel 4: The Slaying of Ishbosheth

points: They remembered that even when Saul was king, David was the one that led them out and brought them in as captain, for David fought many wars and had fame among the people. The Lord had said unto David that he should feed His people Israel and be a captain over Israel.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

points: Michal, Saul's daughter, looked through a window and saw David leaping and dancing before the Lord, and she despised him in her heart. This is a spirit to be careful of: coming out of the spirit on the Lord's day and murmuring against a brother who is rejoicing in the Most High.

note.label: 2 Samuel 6: David Brings Up the Ark of God

points: Michal, the daughter of Saul, had no child unto the day of her death; the Lord shut her womb. Do not play with the Most High.

note.label: 2 Samuel 6: David Brings Up the Ark of God

points: David asked whether there was yet any left of the house of Saul that he might show him kindness for Jonathan's sake. Remember that Saul's son Jonathan and David were always very close.
That closeness goes back to the beef between Saul and David in the book of Samuel; Jonathan was always there for David, that was David's homeboy, they were really close.

note.label: 2 Samuel 9: David Shows Kindness for Jonathan's Sake

points: A servant of the house of Saul named Ziba was brought to David. When David asked whether there was yet any of the house of Saul that he might show the kindness of God unto him, Ziba said Jonathan had yet a son who was lame on his feet, dwelling in the house of Machir the son of Ammiel in Lodebar.

note.label: 2 Samuel 9: David Shows Kindness for Jonathan's Sake

points: To show his love for Jonathan, David gave everything that Saul owned to Jonathan's son.

note.label: 2 Samuel 9: David Shows Kindness for Jonathan's Sake

points: When Mephibosheth the son of Jonathan came unto David he fell on his face and did reverence. David told him, Fear not, for I will surely show thee kindness for Jonathan thy father's sake, and will restore thee all the land of Saul thy father, and thou shalt eat bread at my table continually.

note.label: 2 Samuel 9: David Shows Kindness for Jonathan's Sake

points: Nathan said unto David, Thou art the man. Thus saith the Most High: I anointed thee king over Israel, delivered thee out of the hand of Saul, gave thee thy master's house and wives, and the house of Israel and of Judah, and would have given thee more. Wherefore hast thou despised the commandment to do evil, killing Uriah the Hittite with the sword and taking his wife, slaying him with the sword of the children of Ammon?

The Most High said if David would have just asked, He would have given him anything, for He had already given him the kingdom, Saul's house, and protection from Saul. The commandment David despised was what was read in Deuteronomy 27. There is a term called suicide by cop; David committed murder by the hand of another nation, because he set the whole thing up.

note.label: 2 Samuel 12: Nathan's Parable and the Judgment on David's House

points: And when king David came to Bahurim, behold, thence came out a man of the family of the house of Saul, whose name was Shimei, the son of Gera: he came forth, and cursed still as he came.

So David saw this as an opportunity to turn back to the Lord, repenting for what he did to Uriah. But what I want you to see is, whether it be lust and covetousness, then came about the hatred to the point where you wanted to put that brother to death, and did. The same exact way envy, jealousy, rebellion against God caused King Saul to do it to King David. So everyone has their path, but that icing on the cake is bitterness for everyone.

note.label: The Building Blocks of Bitterness

points: Shimei was of the house of Saul, and Saul was the wicked one who tried to kill David; it was by the hand of the Most High that Saul did not succeed. Yet Shimei cursed David as if David were in the wrong, because word gets around, people gossip and blame, and he saw David at a low state and went to rub it in his face. That is the mindset of some people in Israel as well.

note.label: 2 Samuel 16: Ziba, Shimei's Cursing, and Absalom Defiles the Concubines

points: The Lord hath returned upon thee all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose stead thou hast reigned; and the Lord hath delivered the kingdom into the hand of Absalom thy son. So here it is. This brother from the house of Saul, meaning from the tribe of Benjamin, is now showing his hatred or disdain for King David for the kingdom being translated over to him. He is blaming King David for Saul's death. He is blaming King David for everything. And in that anger he begins to cast stones at David and his mighty men. Now he is saying, the fact that Absalom is hunting for you, you deserve it, because of all the bloodiness that you did. Now Absalom is doing it to you.

note.label: The Building Blocks of Bitterness

points: As David came to Bahurim, a man of the house of Saul named Shimei the son of Gera came out, cursing and casting stones at David and all his servants. Shimei cursed, calling David a bloody man and a man of Belial, saying the Most High had returned upon him all the blood of the house of Saul, and delivered the kingdom into the hand of Absalom his son, and taken him in his mischief because he was a bloody man.

note.label: 2 Samuel 16: Ziba, Shimei's Cursing, and Absalom Defiles the Concubines

points: Shimei the son of Gera the Benjamite hastened down with a thousand men of Benjamin, along with Ziba the servant of Saul's house with his sons and servants, and fell down before the king at Jordan.

note.label: 2 Samuel 19: The King Returns to His House

points: Mephibosheth the son of Saul came down to meet the king, having neither dressed his feet, trimmed his beard, nor washed his clothes from the day the king departed until he returned in peace, showing his mourning for David.

note.label: 2 Samuel 19: The King Returns to His House

points: There was a famine in the days of David, three years, year after year, and David inquired of the Lord. The Lord answered that it was for Saul and for his bloody house, because he slew the Gibeonites. Saul broke his word. The Gibeonites were not of the children of Israel but of the remnant of the Amorites, and Israel had sworn unto them, yet Saul sought to slay them in his zeal.

note.label: 2 Samuel 21: The Famine, the Gibeonites, and the Sons of the Giant

points: The lesson the Most High is teaching Israel here is to pay what you vow. Let your yea be yea and your nay be nay; Saul went back on his word after he had given his yea to the Amorites, and the whole house paid for it.

note.label: 2 Samuel 21: The Famine, the Gibeonites, and the Sons of the Giant

points: David asked the Gibeonites what he should do and wherewith he should make the atonement. The blessing was not truly coming from the Gibeonites who are of Ammon; it was coming from the Most High, who was teaching Israel a lesson through this famine. The Gibeonites would take no silver nor gold of Saul nor of his house, but asked for seven of Saul's sons to be hanged unto the Lord in Gibeah of Saul.

note.label: 2 Samuel 21: The Famine, the Gibeonites, and the Sons of the Giant

points: The king spared Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, because of the Lord's oath that was between David and Jonathan. David did not go back on his oath; earlier he had promised Jonathan that his seed would always eat at David's table as long as there was family of the lineage of Jonathan.

note.label: 2 Samuel 21: The Famine, the Gibeonites, and the Sons of the Giant

points: Jonathan's body had been hanged in the temple of Dagon, the fish god of the Hamites. David buried the bones of Saul and Jonathan in the country of Benjamin in Zelah, in the sepulchre of Kish his father, and performed all that the king commanded. After that the Most High was entreated for the land.

note.label: 2 Samuel 21: The Famine, the Gibeonites, and the Sons of the Giant

points: David spoke unto the Lord the words of this song in the day the Lord had delivered him out of the hand of all his enemies and out of the hand of Saul. He called the Lord his rock, his fortress, and his deliverer, his shield and the horn of his salvation, his high tower and his refuge, his saviour who saved him from violence.

note.label: 2 Samuel 22: The Lord Is My Rock and My Fortress

points: The chapter returns to Gibeon and repeats the line of Ner, Kish, and Saul, tracing Saul's sons and the house of Jonathan down through Micah to Azel.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 9: The Returned Inhabitants and Their Offices

points: The battle went hard against Saul, the archers wounded him, and he asked his armourbearer to run him through so the uncircumcised would not abuse him. The armourbearer was too afraid, so Saul fell on his own sword and died.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 10: The Death of Saul

points: Saul died, his three sons, and all his house together, and when Israel saw it they forsook their cities and fled, and the Philistines came and dwelt in them.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 10: The Death of Saul

points: When Jabesh-gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul, all their valiant men arose, took the bodies of Saul and his sons, brought them to Jabesh, buried their bones under the oak, and fasted seven days.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 10: The Death of Saul

points: Saul died for his transgression against the Most High, for not keeping His word, and for asking counsel of one that had a familiar spirit rather than inquiring of the Most High. Therefore the Most High slew him and turned the kingdom to David the son of Jesse.

Saul had gone to a woman with a familiar spirit to bring up Samuel. The left hand of the Most High is real. People who meddle with that get entangled and get spirits put on them. It is not our custom.
The last straw for Saul was seeking that familiar spirit. Through Samuel the Most High told him he would join him the next day. The difference is that Samuel died righteously.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 10: The Death of Saul

points: These came to David at Ziklag while he kept himself close because of Saul. They were mighty helpers of the war, armed with bows, able to use both the right hand and the left in hurling stones and shooting arrows.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 12: The Tribes Gather to David

points: They were of Saul's own brethren of Benjamin. Benjamin always had the reputation of being ambidextrous, able to hurl a stone with either hand and hit a hair's breadth.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 12: The Tribes Gather to David

points: Some of Manasseh fell to David; they had come with the Philistines against Saul but did not help them, for the Philistine lords sent them away, fearing he would return to Saul at the jeopardy of their heads.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 12: The Tribes Gather to David

points: These are the numbers of the armed bands that came to David at Hebron to turn Saul's kingdom to him according to the word of the Most High, tribe by tribe.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 12: The Tribes Gather to David

points: His purpose was to bring again the ark of the Most High, for they had not inquired at it in the days of Saul. All the congregation agreed, for the thing was right in the eyes of all the people.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 13: Bringing Up the Ark

points: Michal the daughter of Saul looked out the window and despised David in her heart as he danced and played. In the midst of pure righteousness she was out of the spirit, hating him instead of rejoicing.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 15: None Ought to Carry the Ark but the Levites

points: To the chief musician, Maschil, a Psalm of David, written when Doeg the Edomite came and told Saul that David had come to the house of Ahimelech. Why boastest thou thyself in mischief, O mighty man?

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

points: To the chief musician on Neginoth, Maschil, a Psalm of David, when the Ziphims came and said to Saul, Doth not David hide himself with us? Save me, O God, by thy name, and judge me by thy strength.

note.label: Psalm 54: Save Me by Thy Name

points: And afterward they desired a king: and God gave unto them Saul the son of Cis, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, by the space of forty years. So this is who the Lord established, because of what we wanted. So even though we wanted a king, it was still the Lord that had to establish that.

And when he had removed him. So when who had removed him? When the Lord removed Saul from being king over Israel. So where does this power and authority come from? Only of God. Only God can make you sovereign and remove your sovereignty. It is only God, not you or your piece of paper with weird words on it.

note.label: Sovereign Idiocracy
